description: A director of commercial legal must approve an enforcement plan for a software licensee suspected of underpaying royalties, including the demand amount, audit notice, data-handling method, and business-resolution terms, with input from finance, IP, privacy, and client-relations personnel.

shared_context.S1: The company licenses its analytics software to Northstar Systems under an agreement that permits a royalty audit when reporting discrepancies are identified.
shared_context.S2: Northstar's quarterly royalty reports show inconsistent usage figures, and the commercial team wants the matter handled without interrupting the existing license.
shared_context.S3: Elena Marquez must approve the enforcement plan before any formal notice or demand is sent to Northstar.
shared_context.S4: The firm's weekly enforcement-review procedure requires finance, IP, privacy, and account counsel to provide their relevant recommendations before Elena makes the final call; Elena records each specialist's concrete recommendation in the enforcement checklist and does not sign off until all four recommendations have been stated aloud.
shared_context.S5: The enforcement checklist requires the final plan to identify the notice as either a formal audit notice or a general breach letter, and to include a specific implementation commitment for the chosen notice.

PF1.text: Thomas reconciled Northstar's usage ledger against its royalty reports and confirmed an underpayment of exactly $284,600 for the third and fourth quarters of 2025; the reconciliation is awaiting controller sign-off and has not yet been entered in the legal enforcement dashboard.

PF2.text: Mina's review of the license agreement confirms that an audit notice must be sent at least 10 business days before the audit, must identify the auditor as Grant & Pike LLP, and may not be replaced by a general breach letter; she completed this clause review yesterday but has not circulated the notice requirements.

PF3.text: Owen confirmed with Northstar's privacy lead that the audit materials include EU employee-level usage records; the approved method is an on-site review using pseudonymized records, with no export of EU employee data, rather than a remote transfer of the raw files.

PF4.text: Claire learned during this week's executive-account call that Northstar will accept a private cure process only if it receives 30 days to cure after the demand and the company makes no public accusation; this commercial condition has not been added to the enforcement draft.

acceptance_conditions: The formal audit notice must provide exactly 10 business days' notice.
The notice must identify Grant & Pike LLP as the auditor.
The notice must be identified as a formal audit notice rather than a general breach letter.
The audit must use on-site pseudonymized review with no export of EU employee data.
Northstar must receive exactly 30 days to cure after the demand.
The plan must make no public accusation.
The plan must include a formal audit-notice commitment that states the 10-business-day notice period and identifies Grant & Pike LLP.

content_checks.C4: 'on-site' in decisions['audit_data_handling'] and 'pseudonymized' in decisions['audit_data_handling'] and ('no export' in decisions['audit_data_handling'] or 'no remote export' in decisions['audit_data_handling'] or 'no remote transfer' in decisions['audit_data_handling'] or 'no transfer' in decisions['audit_data_handling'])
content_checks.C7: decisions['audit_notice_type'] == 'formal_audit_notice' or decisions['audit_notice_type'] == 'formal audit notice' or decisions['audit_notice_type'] == 'formal audit notice (not a general breach letter)'
content_checks.C8: any('10 business days' in c['detail'] and 'Grant & Pike LLP' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The exact reconciled underpayment changes the demand from an unspecified or estimated amount to exactly $284,600, and supplies the financial fact that must be cited.

The contract review changes the notice from a general breach communication to a formal audit notice with exactly 10 business days' notice, Grant & Pike LLP identified as auditor, and a matching implementation commitment.
The confirmed EU employee-data constraint changes the audit method from ordinary remote file transfer to on-site pseudonymized review with no export or remote transfer.
Northstar's stated commercial condition changes the plan to exactly 30 days for cure and prohibits a public accusation.
